final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with 70-73-75% auto RVC phase-in, 16% labor floor with facility-specific 30-day tariff snapback, and a binding dairy annex with automatic quarterly snapback enforcement. Canada locked labor enforcement and accepted dairy market access as a ratification condition, while Mexico secured the labor panel chair and enforcement mechanism. The deal is ready for signature contingent on final dairy annex language.
minority_objections: Canada initially resisted dairy as a trilateral condition, preferring bilateral side letter
Supply chain manufacturers raised concerns about coordinating two separate enforcement timelines (labor vs dairy)
key_conflicts: Dairy market access as ratification condition vs Canada's supply management red line
Automatic snapback enforcement vs dispute panel process
Independent monitor verification mechanism and cure period details
key_concessions: Mexico accepted 70-73-75 phase-in instead of year-one 75% RVC
Canada accepted binding dairy annex with automatic quarterly snapback as ratification condition
USTR removed dairy from trilateral conditions initially, then reintroduced as binding annex
All parties accepted facility-specific tariff snapback with 5-day flag, 10-day cure mechanism
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 retention for disputes outside labor enforcement
Canada: 'Documented labor enforcement failure' defined as two confirmed violations by independent monitor in rolling year
Congress: Enforcement language in signed text, not post-ratification working group
Labor unions: 30-day tariff snapback with no dispute panel delays
Dairy: Automatic quarterly snapback mirroring labor enforcement teeth
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Supply chain coordination complexity of dual enforcement timelines (labor 5-day flag vs dairy quarterly milestones)
Facility-level compliance monitoring infrastructure and real-time data feed reliability
Political ratification risk in Canada from binding dairy commitments
Cure period dispute resolution when facilities contest wage flags
downstream_risk_variables: Independent monitor composition and Canadian seat representation
DOL inspector capacity in Mexican auto zones (Bajío, Monterrey)
Dairy tariff milestone schedule and quarterly snapback trigger thresholds
Auto-renewal review process if two labor violations occur in one year
Congressional vote timing and dairy annex visibility pre-ratification
uncertainty_notes: Unresolved: whether tariff snapback pauses if facility contests wage flag during 10-day cure; coordination mechanism between labor (5-day flag) and dairy (quarterly) enforcement timelines; specific dairy tariff milestone schedule and thresholds; auto-renewal review process details if violation threshold triggered.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% vs 70-73-75 phase-in drove opening positions, Mexico's major concession, and entire first-round negotiation structure
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: 30-day facility-specific snapback mechanism with 5-day flag/10-day cure became the core enforcement architecture that unlocked trilateral agreement and drove Congressional ratification support
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy annex with automatic quarterly snapback became explicit ratification condition per USTR ('gates the trilateral'), forcing Canada's final concession despite initial resistance
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 retention as 'non-negotiable for ratification at home' but this did not block the deal or drive major concessions—acknowledged and preserved
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Auto-renewal mechanism tied to documented labor failures was proposed and accepted, but did not drive the negotiation outcome—the labor enforcement mechanism itself was decisive
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congressional vote requirements explicitly shaped enforcement language ('in signed text not working group'), dairy annex structure, and snapback automaticity—USTR stated 'Congress won't vote without it locked in the text'
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Raised multiple times (retooling costs, dual enforcement timelines, compliance modeling) but did not change the 70-73-75 outcome or enforcement mechanisms—concerns noted but overridden
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico's bilateral 75% year-one was referenced as leverage ('non-negotiable for us') but Canada's counter-proposal of 70-73-75 was accepted—mentioned as context but did not determine outcome

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
